paragraphs: Marine biologists studying a protected reef off a tropical island report that its fish population has tripled in the decade since fishing was banned there. They conclude that the ban was responsible, and they recommend similar bans for neighboring reefs. The conclusion is plausible, but it rests on a comparison with the reef's own condition before the ban, not on a comparison with unprotected reefs over the same decade. If fish numbers rose across the whole region during those years, for instance because of a change in ocean temperature or in the supply of larvae, then the ban might deserve little of the credit.
